rows.en:
So I'm the one telling the third story.
I'm Akemi Iwashita.
...Very well, I'll tell it to you.
{a}{f:|}?{p}Do you like paintings?
I like them
I don't like them
Neither, really

...I see.
Paintings are wonderful, aren't they?
I like them too.
I'm especially fond of Dali's paintings.
Paintings give us a world of fantasy.
They soothe the heart so.
People who can paint are marvelous.
{a}{f:|}.{p}Do you paint or draw often?
I do
Not very often

...I see.
That's a fine thing.
What sort of pictures do you make, I wonder?
I'd like you to show me some time.
It's a promise.
You absolutely must show me.
They say a picture reflects the heart and character of the one who made it.
When I look at a picture, I can tell what that person is feeling inside.{p}

Paintings are alive, you know.
If you pour your whole heart and soul into the painting you're working on, a soul will always find its way into it.
...Whatever kind of painting it may be.
Even in this world, you know, there are many paintings full of resentment still left behind.
Though they're rarely put on show in museums and the like.
People who paint often don't live comfortably, do they?
The artistic temperament, I suppose you'd call it.
It's different if they paint for a living, but people who paint what they like, the way they like, often can't make ends meet, I hear.
Of course, it's the path they chose, and they do it because they love it, so no one can complain.
But you see, among them are some whose discontent turns into resentment, and who hurl those feelings onto the canvas.
Even after that person dies, a painting possessed by their grudge remains forever.
In an attic studio in some abandoned house, the grudge of a painter no one ever recognized waits, aimlessly, silently, though no one will ever come.{p}

Ufufu... imagining things like that is delightful.
What I'm going to tell you now is the story of a single painting...
If you like paintings, why didn't you join the art club?
If you'd joined the art club, you'd have encountered so many lovely paintings.
Our school's art club is quite famous, you know.
Masumura, our art teacher, has been selected at well-known competitions many times, and often holds solo exhibitions.
They say several of the art club's graduates are already making a living as professionals.
You've at least heard the name Takaaki Komatsuzawa, that illustrator who's been in the news so often lately, haven't you?
Apparently that illustrator is one of our graduates too.{p}

Oil paintings, watercolors, sketches that people like that made in their high school days... a great many of those keepsake pictures are stored away in this school.
Pictures like those must be packed with hopes and dreams.
But you know, they aren't all like that.
Paintings like the ones I told you about a moment ago.
Yes, paintings that seem to hold a person's grudge.
There are some like that in our school, too.{p}

You know that a number of paintings by art club members hang in the art room, don't you?
Most of what's on display now is the work of current members, but there are also works by seniors who won all sorts of prizes.
But those are only a small part.
Just a handful of works, chosen from more paintings than anyone could count.
Do you know what becomes of the works that aren't chosen?
The members take most of them home, but not all of them.
Works that seem forgotten even by the ones who made them.
Those are piled up in a corner of the art club's room, gathering dust.
It's a pitiful thing.
When paintings are alive too.
Among them, you see, there is just one painting that its creator loved, and yet it still had to meet that miserable fate.
Why, you ask?{p}
Ufufu...{p}Before I tell you that story, if you don't mind, shall we all go and take a look at the art club's room now?
Let's go and see
I won't go
I'll stay here

Ufufu...
Of course.
After all, you love paintings, {a}{f:|}.
I just knew you'd say that.{p}

Well then, everyone, let's move.
...Don't worry.
I have the key to the club room.
Why do I have it, you ask?
I'll leave that to your imagination.{p}

...Here we are.
It's in here.
I'll show you all that painting.
You see, I get to look at it now and then.
At that painting.
So I know where it is.{p}

There, it's among those canvases piled up over there.
...Yes, that third oil painting.
Take it out.
Handle it with care.{p}

...This portrait of a woman.
What do you all think?
Do you feel anything?
What about you, {a}{f:|}?{p}Do you sense something?
I don't feel anything in particular
It's creepy

Is that so?
What a rude thing to say.
Fufu... but, well, never mind.
Most people who see this painting say that.{p}

This is a pitiful painting.
A pitiful painting that never gets to see the light of day.
Since we've come all this way, let's hang this painting in the art room, if only for a little while.
All right?{p}We can hang it, can't we, {a}{f:|}?
It's fine to hang it
We shouldn't hang it

Ufufu... thank you.
I'm sure the painting is happy too.
I can hear it.
The painting, saying thank you.
Let's hang it in the spot where it stands out the most.
Let's see... there would be good.{p}
You'd never think a grudge was dwelling in it, would you?{p}

...Well then, shall we go back?
Don't worry.
I'll make sure to lock both the art room and the club room.

I'm sorry, everyone.
It seems I dragged you all along on my selfish whim.{p}{a}{f:|}, are you angry?
I'm angry
I'm not angry

I see, I'm glad.
Of course you aren't. They do say people who love paintings are kind.{p}
...Well then, now that everyone has taken their seats, shall we go on with the story?{p}

The person who painted that picture, you see, is the very woman in the portrait.
A self-portrait, in other words.
She was a student at our school long ago.
Naturally, she was in the art club.
Her name was Tomoko Shimizu.{p}

Shimizu was a gentle, quiet person, I hear.
She was reserved, and was always at her canvas, painting.
She loved painting, and was aiming for art college.
But that dream never came true.{p}
Because she died right after she painted that picture.{p}

...She was murdered.
No one knows who killed her, even now.
The culprit was never caught.
It seems someone strangled her to death on her way home from school.
Perhaps it was a random attacker.
Or perhaps it was planned...
Shimizu had been working so hard on that painting, you see.
The prefectural competition was coming up.
To enter it, she stayed late in the art room, finishing that painting.{p}

...And then, just before the painting was finished, the tragedy happened.
Perhaps it was because she stayed at school painting so late.
If she'd gone home early, the tragedy might never have happened.
And so, that painting was left unfinished.
Ufufu... yes, in truth, that painting was never completed.
She was killed with it still unfinished.
...But that painting is finished, isn't it?
Do you know why?{p}

Even after she died, you see, she kept on painting it.
After the incident, her half-finished painting was kept in the art room.
Her family agreed that would be for the best.
And the unfinished portrait was hung in the most prominent spot in the whole art room.{p}

...And then, some time after that, a rumor gradually began to spread.
That the portrait was being completed, little by little, every day.{p}

When people looked with that in mind, the painting really had changed from how it was at first.
The talk was that someone must be secretly working on the painting when no one was around.
But even when the art room was locked, the painting had always been worked on.
So everyone whispered about it.
Her ghost must be coming out to paint it, they said.
And then one of the art club members who'd been close to Shimizu tried to find out for sure.{p}

And that member saw it.
Shimizu's figure, standing motionless, staring at the painting.{p}

Though no one carried it there, the painting would end up hanging in the art room all by itself before anyone knew it.
No matter how many times they put it away, the painting was somehow back in the art room.
As if it wanted everyone to look at it.
Because it was so creepy, the school contacted her family and had them take it home.
But even then, it was no use.
The painting, taken home, would somehow come back to the art room on its own.
Perhaps she loved that art room dearly.
Or perhaps there was some other reason...
Fufufu...
Some suggested burning the painting.
But everyone was too afraid of being cursed to do it.
Then came the idea of simply having a memorial service held for it.{p}So in the end, what do you think they did?
They burned it
They tore it up
They held a memorial service

In the end, they called in a Buddhist priest to hold a memorial service.
...But it was no use.
Perhaps her spirit's attachment was stronger.
No matter how many services they held, the painting kept flying back to the art room.
So, with nothing more they could do, they decided to leave it alone.
It wasn't doing any harm, after all.
For the time being, if finishing the painting would satisfy her, they decided to watch over it warmly.
The painting came closer to completion, little by little, every day.
So slightly you could hardly tell the difference.
And then the painting was finished.{p}

A beautiful self-portrait of Shimizu was complete.
And the moment the painting was finished, this time it vanished from the art room.{p}

Once it was gone, that was eerie in its own way.
Though they'd been so frightened of it, now they started searching for the painting.{p}
Where do you think the painting was?
Her house
The club room
Her grave
I have no idea

Ufufu... I see.
You can't guess?{p}

The painting, you see, had been left at the place where she was killed.
The person who found it was shocked.
The painting had changed beyond recognition.
The beautiful portrait was twisted in agony and deathly pale.
Blood dripped from the mouth, and the eyes bulged so far they looked about to fall out.
That face was Shimizu's face at the moment she was killed.
At some point, the face painted in the portrait had changed.
The finished painting had been beautiful, but now it was a horrible sight.
It seemed to resent that the killer had never been caught, as if it were trying to tell someone something.{p}
And then the school took the painting back once again.{p}

But you know, they say that sometimes the painting takes on the face she had when she was killed.
It's only a rumor, and I haven't seen it even once myself yet...
They say that especially when someone talks about Shimizu, the painting grieves and changes into that face.

I wonder how it is right now?
If you like, shall we go and look at it in the art room now?{p}The face might have changed.
I'll go and look
I won't go and look
I'll stay behind by myself

Come, let's go.
We might get to see the face Shimizu made as she died in agony.
Scared?
There's nothing to be scared of, is there?
After all, you had nothing to do with Shimizu's murder.
Look, the art room is drawing nearer and nearer.
Seeing it like this, don't you feel as if something unclean is seeping out of that art room?
I can see it clearly.
Something like a pitch-black mist is crawling out through the gap in the tightly shut door, as if it were writhing.
Now, ready?
I'm going to open the door.
Once I open the door, you'll see that painting.
Now, ready?
I'm opening it.
...Good.{p}

Wait a moment.
Before I open it, let me tell you just one thing.
About that painting of hers, the one that had changed so horribly, lying where Shimizu was killed...

For some reason, everyone who saw it died.
The person who found the painting, and the students who happened to see it at school, too.{p}

Of course, it might just be a string of coincidences.
After all, only four people have died so far.
...But the way they died was abnormal.
Every one of them strangled themselves to death.
How agonizing that must have been.
Strangling yourself with your own hands...
Even for a suicide, I've never heard of such a thing.
And the faces of the people who died that way were all twisted in agony and pale, just like that painting, they say.
As if Shimizu had cursed them to death...
As if Shimizu, lonely all by herself, wanted friends...
I can't believe it's mere coincidence.
She's made four friends now, but I'm sure Shimizu is still lonely...
I'm sorry.
For spoiling such a pleasant moment.
Now, are you ready?
Have you prepared yourself?
What sort of face will the portrait beyond this door have, I wonder?
I can hardly wait...{p}
{a}{f:|}?{p}What sort of face would you prefer?
